title: Damage and lost property
audience: Short-stay turnover cleaners who may find damage or lost property during a turnover.
learningOutcomes: Record damage found during a turnover, separating it from cleaning issues.
Handle lost property so that it is recorded, secured and returned through the approved route.
Avoid accusations and avoid repairing damage yourself.

instruction.heading: Recording damage as you find it
instruction.body: Damage is anything that has been broken, marked, cracked, chipped, torn, burnt, stained into the material or left missing. Record it at the moment you see it, before you clean around it. Write the location in the property, a short factual description, and the time. Take a photograph where the property rules allow it, with the item in view and a reference point so that the place can be found again. Separate damage from cleaning issues in the record. A stain that remains after a proper clean is a cleaning issue if it comes off with the approved method, and a damage issue if it is part of the surface, such as a mark that has soaked into timber or a burn on a benchtop. Do not repair the damage yourself, and do not try to hide it under a mat, a towel or a cushion. A hidden damage item becomes the cleaner's problem later, and it is a false record.

instruction.heading: Lost property: recording, securing and returning
instruction.body: Lost property is any item that is not rubbish and is not the property's own fixed contents, such as a phone, a bag, keys, clothing or jewellery. When you find it, stop and record it: the item, its description, the exact location where you found it, the time, and your name. Secure the item in the approved place, in a sealed bag or container where the procedure requires one, with a reference number that matches the record. Keep a simple chain of custody, which means the record shows who held the item and when. Pass the item through the approved return route, which is the coordinator or the property manager, not a guest you happen to meet. Do not look through personal items beyond what you need to identify and record them. For example, you may note that a phone is in a case with a particular colour, but you should not unlock it, read messages or photograph its contents. Never keep an item, even for a short time, and never take it home.

instruction.heading: Keeping the record factual and avoiding accusations
instruction.body: Record what you found and when you found it, and leave the attribution of damage to the coordinator and the property manager. Do not state who caused the damage, do not guess at the cause, and do not write opinions about the guest. A record such as 'cracked tile at the base of the shower wall, approximately one finger-width crack, photographed at 10:40' is useful. A record such as 'the guest broke this tile' is not, because the cleaner did not see it happen. If the damage looks like a safety hazard, such as broken glass or exposed wiring, make the area safe first, keep people away, and report it at once. Do not clean up broken glass with bare hands. Send the record through the approved channel, and keep a copy in the turnover log.

procedure: Record each item of damage with its location, a short factual description, the time, and a photograph where the property rules allow it.
Separate each damage item from cleaning issues in the record, and do not repair or hide any item.
Stop and record each lost item with its description, location, time and your name.
Secure the lost item in the approved place, in a sealed container where required, with a reference that matches the record.
Pass the item through the approved return route, and record the handover.
Do not state who caused the damage, and make any hazardous area safe before you leave it.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner finds a cracked bathroom tile and a phone under a bed during a turnover.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you record and do?
workedExamples.reasoning: Record the cracked tile with its location and a photograph as damage, and do not repair it. Record the phone with its description, the bedroom location and the time, secure it in the approved place with a matching reference, and pass it to the approved return route. Do not unlock the phone or read its messages. Do not state who caused the crack.

workedExamples.situation: During the scan, a cleaner finds a drinking glass broken on the kitchen floor and a shard under the cabinet.
workedExamples.reasoning: Keep people and bare feet away from the area. Do not pick up the glass with bare hands. Use the tools and the cut-resistant gloves the business procedure sets, and clear the larger pieces into a rigid container. Record the location, the time and the state of the floor, and report the damage to the coordinator. Do not state who broke the glass.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner finds a wedding ring in a bathroom drawer and a guest's name appears on the booking handover.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Is the name on the booking enough to return the ring?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. Record the item, the location and the time, and secure it. Pass it to the coordinator through the approved route, so that the return is arranged and recorded. Do not contact the guest directly unless the procedure tells you to. Do not keep the ring, and do not put it back in the drawer.

equipmentAndPpe: Damage record form, with fields for location, description, time and photograph reference.
Lost-property log, sealable bags or containers, and reference labels.
Secure storage for lost items, as the property procedure sets.
Cut-resistant gloves for broken glass, as the business procedure sets, and a rigid container for debris.
Camera for permitted photographs, used before any clean-up of the item.

commonErrors.prevention: Record it and report it for repair.

commonErrors.error: Cleaning away a mark before it is photographed or recorded.
commonErrors.prevention: Record and photograph the damage first, then clean around it if the procedure allows.

commonErrors.error: Keeping a found item, or returning it to the first guest you see.
commonErrors.prevention: Record, secure and pass the item through the approved route.

commonErrors.error: Searching through personal items beyond what identification needs.
commonErrors.prevention: Note only the description needed to identify the item, and stop there.

commonErrors.error: Blaming a guest for the damage.
commonErrors.prevention: Record what you found and leave attribution to the coordinator.

commonErrors.error: Handling broken glass with bare hands.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep people away, use the approved gloves and tools, and report the damage.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Found property. Rules for handling found property, including how long it is held and how it is returned, are set by the state or territory and by the business and property procedures.
Personal information. Records and photographs of guests' belongings are personal information. Limit records and photographs to what the procedure requires.

Broken glass and exposed hazards are handled first for safety. The steps in this lesson are the minimum the cleaner takes before the coordinator decides on repair. This lesson does not grant any authority to repair a fitting, a wiring fault or a gas fitting.
No official source was used for this lesson.

qualityStandard: Damage is recorded separately from cleaning issues, with location, description, time and photograph where permitted.
Lost property is recorded, secured with a matching reference, and passed through the approved route with the handover recorded.
Nothing is repaired, kept or hidden, and the record contains no attribution statement.
Hazards such as broken glass are made safe before the cleaner moves on.
documentationEvidence: Damage record with location, description, time and photograph reference.
Lost-property record with item, location, time, finder and reference number.
Handover record showing who received the lost item and when.
summary: Record damage as found, and keep it separate from cleaning issues.
Secure lost property, and pass it through the approved route with a handover record.
Do not repair, keep, or assign blame for damage.

knowledgeChecks.question: You find a cracked tile during a turnover. What is correct?
options: Record it as damage, with its location, and report it
Repair it quickly with some glue and a clean cloth today
Hide it under a mat until the end of the stay today

knowledgeChecks.question: You find a phone during a turnover. What is correct?
options: Keep it safe in your bag until the end of the day today
Record it, secure it and pass it through the approved route
Return it to the first guest you see in the house on the day

knowledgeChecks.question: Should the record say who caused a damaged fitting?
options: Yes, name the last guest who stayed in the room before you arrived
Yes, if you are sure of who caused the damage to the fitting
No, record what was found and leave attribution to the coordinator
